::: {.callout-important title="Complete content draft — release candidate 2"}
This document contains **all eight chapters** of *Modern LLM
Architecture: A Visual Guide to Attention, Memory, Sparsity, and Hybrid
Models* (workbook 04 of the ML/LLM Study Workbooks series) -- a
release candidate, not the final edition. Every chapter was first
drafted, illustrated, and validated individually; this revision then
completed a whole-book editorial, cross-reference, and visual-production
pass across all eight chapters together: a notation-table layout
defect, an orphan page, a title line-break, and the chapter/answer-key
numbering scheme were each found and corrected, and terminology,
cross-references, and page breaks were checked across the assembled
document rather than chapter by chapter in isolation. Treat this as a
complete, reviewed content draft -- still not a final, professionally
copy-edited book, since no substitute exists for an independent human
proofread pass beyond what this project's own automated and visual
checks can catch.

Multi-head latent attention (MLA), briefly deferred out of Chapter 3's
drafting pass, is covered in Chapter 4 alongside sliding-window and
sparse attention. Chapter 4 covers recurrent/state-space/linear-attention
alternatives only as a brief taxonomy and forward reference; Chapter 6
adds the primary source that taxonomy was pending (Gu and Dao's
selective state-space mechanism) once a hybrid case study needed it.
Chapter 5 covers mixture-of-experts architecture only -- detailed
distributed-training implementation, collective-communication
algorithms, kernel optimization, inference-engine configuration,
expert quantization, model-specific benchmark comparisons,
post-training, and routing-research surveys are all deferred to later
workbooks. Chapter 6 selects exactly three real, pinned model families
(Llama 3 405B, DeepSeek-V3, Jamba) as case studies -- not a survey of
every current model, not a benchmark ranking, and not a release-history
timeline. Chapter 7 synthesizes systems consequences already implied
by Chapters 2-6 (a resource ledger, prefill-vs-decode, an
architecture-to-systems consequence map, and a minimal parallelism
overview) and previews looped depth in one row only. Chapter 8 gives
looped depth/recurrent depth its full treatment (this workbook's
assigned primary home for that topic) and closes with a 10-question
synthesis framework -- it does not teach multi-token prediction's
training mechanics or the speculative-decoding algorithm, both
assigned to future workbooks in this series' own cross-workbook topic
roadmap. Public reporting has associated recurrent depth with a model
referred to as "GPT-6 Astra"; no official technical source confirms
this, and this workbook does not treat that proprietary architecture
as verified anywhere it is mentioned.

This is a review artifact: it exists to establish the workbook's
explanatory depth, visual language, page density, question style, and
citation style. If you still find a rough edge, it is exactly the kind
of thing this pass was built to surface -- report it rather than
assuming it was already caught.
:::
